result:
PR #379 is out of draft and ready to fold. Arm 3, the re-run after merging master, passed 375 of 375 checks, the same result as arm 2.

- **Why the last session didn't finish:** it had stopped, correctly, to wait for arm 3. The arms job queued that arm as `1790426794-arms-tiecode282-*`, and both runs were done by 13:10Z. No `[job.arms]` verdict had been posted, so I judged the pair myself against `tiecode282-merge.json`.
- **Arm 3 numbers:** 139 captures better, 0 worse, 225 unchanged. Exact matches went from 110 to 166, and none regressed from exact. `Pixel_shader` and `Texture_3D_as_2D` are unchanged from master. `Volume_texture` went from 34,727 differing pixels to 0, and `Texture_palette` from 10,488 to 0.
- **Texture render target (row 240):** its separate run on the merge had already passed 68 of 68. All 28 TexFmt_* captures are exact.
- **Master since the merge:** it has 35 new commits. None of them touch `psh.c`, `psh.h`, `geom.c` or `nv2a_index.json`, and a test merge is clean, so I did not merge again or re-run the arm.
- **Definition of done:**
  - Preflight passes on `6321ec4477` (with `--allow-tracker`), and CI was green on the previous head.
  - The PR body's `Files:` line matches the diff against master. It also names `psh.h`, `nv2a_index.json`, `psh_differ/differ.c` and three helper files in `docs/lanes/tiecode282/`, none of which are on the brief's list. `geom.c`, which the brief names, is untouched, because one more flat vertex output would exceed Vulkan's minimum limit for geometry outputs.
  - Section 8b of `docs/lanes/tiecode282/NOTES.md` holds the result and why the last session stopped. The PR body carries the arm 3 result and says `psh.c`/`psh.h` are released, so the BRDF work (#315) can take `psh.c` next.
  - The verdict is posted as a `[lane.tiecode282]` comment.

The rule only applies where the evidence covers it: Vulkan, fixed-function draws, and triangles whose vertices sit upper-left, upper-right and lower-right. Other vertex arrangements are still unmeasured. It is also turned off when either leg of the triangle is a power of two. Arm 1 showed that on those draws the rule predicted the wrong direction: silicon breaks every tie up there.

My arm 3 check printed an `UNBOUND` note: the file was registered before either run, but no queued request names it. The arms job queued this run itself, so I expect its own verdict comment to follow.
